chapter.v:
Honoring someone
stupid is as inappropriate as snow in the summer or rain during harvest.

A curse
that isn't deserved won't land on the person, like a fluttering sparrow or a flitting swallow.

Horses need
a whip, donkeys need a bridle, and stupid people need a rod on their backs!

Don't answer
stupid people following their stupidity, or you'll become as bad as them.

Answer stupid
people following their stupidity, otherwise they'll think they're wise.

Trusting someone
stupid to deliver a message is like cutting off your feet or drinking poison.

A proverb
spoken by someone stupid is as useless as a lame person's legs.

Honoring someone
stupid is as pointless as tying a stone into a sling.

A proverb
spoken by someone stupid is as ridiculous as a thorn bush waved around by a drunk.

Anyone who
hires someone stupid or just a passer-by is like an archer wounding people by shooting arrows at random.

Stupid people
repeat their stupidity like a dog returning to its vomit.

Have you
seen a man who is wise in his own eyes? There's more hope for stupid people than for him!

Lazy people
are the ones who say, “There's a lion on the road—a lion running around the streets!”

A lazy
person turns in bed like a door turns on its hinge.

Lazy people
put their hands in a dish, but are too tired to lift the food to their mouths.

In their
own eyes lazy people are wiser than many sensible advisors.

Interfering in
someone else's quarrel is like grabbing a stray dog by the ears.

You're like
a crazy person firing off blazing arrows and killing people

if you
lie to your friend and then say, “I was only joking!”

Without wood,
the fire goes out; and without gossips, arguments stop.

An argumentative
person fires up quarrels like putting charcoal on hot embers or wood on a fire.

Listening to
gossip is like gulping down bites of your favorite food—they go deep down inside you.

Smooth talking
with evil intent is like a shiny lead glaze on an earthenware pot.

People say
nice things to you even though they hate you; deep down they're just lying to you.

When people
talk nicely to you, don't believe them—their minds are full of hate for you.

Even though
their hatred may be hidden by cunning tricks, their evil will be revealed to everyone.

Those who
dig pits to trap others will fall in themselves, and those who start boulders rolling will be crushed themselves.

If you
tell lies, you show you hate your victims; if you flatter people, you cause disaster.
